name: Shallum
overview: Shallum was a male Levite who served as one of the gatekeepers, specifically stationed at the king's gate. His role as a gatekeeper is noted in several scriptural references, highlighting his responsibility in the security and order of the temple or city gates. His service to the east gate underscores his trusted position among the Levites.
namesAndTitles: The name Shallum means 'peace, well-being, prosperity,' reflecting a desirable state associated with his character or role. He is also known by related names such as Meshelemiah, meaning 'YHWH repays,' Shelemiah, meaning 'YHWH pays back' or possibly 'he restores peace offering of YHWH,' and Meshullam, meaning 'restitution.' These names collectively emphasize themes of divine recompense and restoration.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Shallum as the son of Kore. Various inferred paternal relationships are mentioned, including Zechariah, Mattithiah, Jediael, Zebadiah, Jathniel, Elam, Johanan, Eliehoenai, and Maaseiah, though these are not directly confirmed. These connections suggest Shallum's integration within a broader Levitical lineage.
scriptureSignificance: Shallum's significance lies in his role as a gatekeeper, a vital position entrusted with guarding the temple or city gates, ensuring the sanctity and security of God's dwelling place. His station at the king's gate further indicates a position of honor and responsibility. The multiple names associated with him highlight the theological themes of peace and divine recompense, reinforcing the spiritual importance of his service within the Levitical tribe.
